name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: WACS fault 29 Oct; no new cut found to 21 Nov
summary: No new undersea cable cut or major GNSS jamming escalation found to 21 Nov; WACS repair and Baltic cases continue
state: A fault on the West Africa Cable System segment between the two Congos disrupted circuits on 29 Oct, with a repair ship due on 11 Nov (Tribune Online). A Finnish court jailed the captain and a crew member of the cargo ship Fitburg on 5 Nov for damaging Baltic Sea cables on 31 Dec 2025 (Euronews). Searches on 21 Nov found no new cut and no major new GNSS jamming escalation, so Watch is kept rather than lowered.
for_you: Most users see no effect: traffic reroutes around single cable faults. Repairs can take weeks. Airlines and shipping in the Baltic and eastern Mediterranean remain the most exposed to GNSS interference.
rubric_hit: Watch: cable damage incident (WACS fault 29 Oct) and recent Baltic sabotage convictions; no multiple cuts isolating a region

sources.title: Tribune Online — WACS submarine cable repairs enter critical phase
Euronews — Finnish court jails Russian captain over Baltic Sea cable sabotage

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
